items.title: SPINE: A machine-learning program is on the trail of ghost particles
items.summary: Neutrinos are among the most abundant particles in the universe, but they are also among the most elusive. Nearly massless, they are produced by nuclear reactions in the sun, exploding stars, particle accelerators and even the decay of radioactive elements on Earth. They interact so weakly with ordinary matter that trillions pass through each person every second without leaving a trace. Studying these ghostly particles could help answer some of the biggest questions in physics, from the nature of dark matter to why matter exists at all.

Nothing about the route or his current location has been confirmed, so treat this with some caution until there’s an official word. If it’s accurate, this goes well beyond a losing candidate leaving the country. A presidential runner-up under investigation, travelling without a valid passport, would be landing in a country whose president openly backed him. The family already has a foothold there. His brother Eduardo told Reuters he has received permanent US residency, and has lived in the US since February 2025.

items.summary: Prior was +2.5% y/y 20-city house price index +0.3% m/m vs +0.3% expected Mortgage rates at 7.5% aren't doing any favors for the housing market. For background, the S&P Case-Shiller Home Price Indices are the best-known measure of US house prices. They’re published on the last Tuesday of each month at 9 am ET and carry a roughly two-month lag, so a release in late October covers August. The indexes use a repeat-sales method, tracking price changes on the same single-family homes as they sell over time. Because they compare a property with itself, they avoid the distortions that come from changes in the mix of homes being sold, a weakness of simple median price measures. Each monthly reading is a three-month moving average, which smooths the data but adds to the lag. The headline figure is usually the year-over-year change in the 20-city composite index. October's full Moon, nicknamed the Hunter's Moon, lit up the night sky this weekend. Full Moons throughout the year have traditionally been given names that reflect what is going on in nature . As both parties prepare for the final leg of the campaign, here are some of the most closely watched Senate races. Company says foreign-made robotic vehicles are crucial to US chip production. The uncertainty surrounding the Federal Communications Commission ban on certain foreign-made robots was revealed in the agency’s decision to grant Intel’s waiver request. On October 22, the FCC published its order allowing Intel to continue using the foreign-made robots in US semiconductor manufacturing facilities for a period of one year. The robots in question are automated guided vehicles operating on “tracks or predefined paths” while often requiring operator oversight, according to Intel’s website. They help to move materials and items around within warehouses and factory floors.

Case study gives a whole new meaning to "bedroom eyes." The man in this case was a 71-year-old crop farmer. He told doctors that for the previous two months he had the sensation of having something stuck in both his eyes, which were also red and blurry. When ophthalmologists took a look, they quickly saw the problem: multiple mobile, whitish roundworms. His eyes were not in good shape either, as one might expect. The blood vessels in the membrane over the eye, the conjunctiva, were enlarged, making his eyes look red. And the cells of his cornea—the transparent, dome-shaped outer layer of the eye—had eroded, potentially after the helminths’ hanky-panky.

New contemporary sculpture replaces the globe in the original Roman artifact with a cup as a tribute. The cup is considered one of the seven glass wonders of the world, one of just 40 glass cage cups that survived. Exactly why the unusual color effects of the Lycurgus Cup occurred was a mystery until 2007 , when a team of scientists discovered the color shifts were due to the presence of nanoparticles in the glass—the result of Roman artisans adding finely ground gold and silver into the mix. Those nanoparticles change how the electrons in the cup vibrate in response to light so that the color one sees shifts with the observer’s vantage point.

MyGolfSpy reports golfers should quit apologizing for bad shots, declining bets, or playing from shorter tees to enjoy the game without guilt. Many golfers introduce themselves with a disclaimer about their handicap before the first tee. This habit aims to lower expectations and reassure strangers of their limitations. However, the pressure to apologize for a topped drive or a three-putt is unfounded. Even the best golfers in the world simply want their playing partners to move things along. Speed of play matters more than perfect execution. A bad shot does not require a public statement or a formal apology for taking up space.

Huge software price hikes force loyal users to reconsider their favorite apps. Maybe you’ve used it for years. The UIL approved a phased rollout of a 35-second shot clock for boys and girls varsity basketball beginning no earlier than 2028-29. Police in Brazil say they have cancelled the passports of the defeated right-wing presidential candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, after he failed to comply with an order to surrender the documents. Blue marlin are typically encountered 1,000 miles south off Mexico. Michael Mackenbach hooked the 595-pound blue marlin 12 miles offshore and fought the billfish for 2.5-hours aboard a 20-foot boat. According to BD Outdoors , Mackenbach intended to release the marlin but it died during the fight. Blue marlin are more commonly found in areas off Mexico, such as Cabo San Lucas, nearly 1,000 miles south of San Pedro. Catches off Southern California are exceedingly rare in normal times, when sea-surface temperatures are significantly cooler than the mid-70s still being registered offshore.

Jayden Long and Eddie Hill died after police failed to adequately escalate a dropped 999 call. More people could die on remote mountains unless police do a better job in responding to dropped 999 calls, a coroner has warned. The bodies of friends Eddie Hill, 20, and Jayden Long, 19, both from Dereham, Norfolk, were found on a mountain ridge in Eryri, also known as Snowdonia , on 19 February, a day after a call from Long to North Wales Police was disconnected. Officers did try unsuccessfully to call him back, but then made "limited" efforts to find out who owned the phone and took more than three hours to alert mountain rescue, assistant coroner Sarah Riley said.

Has a team in the World Series ever taken a 3-0 lead and lost the series? The answer is 'not even close,' as it turns out. Whether or not it happens Tuesday at Tropicana Field, history is overwhelmingly on Milwaukee's side. On 25 previous occasions since 1903 when a team went up in the World Series, 3-0, that team won the World Series all 25 times. The only example of a team coming back in a best-of-seven format from a 3-0 deficit was a memorable 2004 Boston Red Sox rally against the New York Yankees , the only time in 43 opportunities that a best-of-seven series featured a team ahead, 3-0, and losing the series. The Red Sox went on to win the World Series.

Overcrowding and poor ventilation caused the deaths of 33 detainees in a prison cell in Minna state. An inquiry into the deaths of 33 detainees in Nigeria's Minna state has found they died as a result of severe overcrowding, poor ventilation and failure by officers to respond to distress calls. Forensic and medical evidence showed the "entirely preventable" deaths had resulted from acute respiratory failure linked to prolonged confinement, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration. The detainees were found dead on 17 September while being held by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps on suspicion of illegal mining. The investigation found that the mining sites had been licensed.
